title: 花犯·咏梅
title_en: To the Tune of Hua Fan: On Plum Blossoms
author: 周邦彦

form.en: ci lyric in two stanzas, 102 characters

text_note.zh: 语料库作“冰盘同宴喜”，通行本作“燕喜”，“燕”通“宴”，意思一样。
text_note.en: The corpus writes the word for feasting with the usual character for a banquet; the common text uses an older character with the same meaning and sound.

readings.zh: 铅华，女子搽脸的粉，“铅”读 qiān。
readings.en: Qiān huá means face powder; the first character is read qiān.

readings.zh: 胜赏，尽情地欣赏美景，“胜”读 shèng。
readings.en: Shèng shǎng means to enjoy a fine sight to the full; the character is read shèng.

readings.zh: 燕喜，宴饮欢乐，“燕”同“宴”，读 yàn。
readings.en: Yàn xǐ means to feast and be merry. The character is used like the word for banquet and is read yàn.
Here the character means soon, right away, and is read xuán.

readings.zh: 相将，将要、就要，“将”读 jiāng。
readings.en: Xiāng jiāng means about to, soon; the second character is read jiāng.
The character is read xié today.

glosses.zh: 粉墙：刷成白色的墙。
glosses.en: fěn qiáng: a whitewashed wall.

glosses.zh: 照眼：花色明亮，映入眼帘。
glosses.en: zhào yǎn: so bright it catches the eye.

glosses.zh: 旧风味：和从前一样的风姿和韵味。
glosses.en: jiù fēng wèi: the same charm and grace as before.

glosses.zh: 轻缀：轻轻地点缀在上面。
glosses.en: qīng zhuì: lightly dotted on.

glosses.zh: 疑：好像。
glosses.en: yí: it seems as if.

glosses.zh: 铅华：女子搽脸的粉。净洗铅华，就是洗去脂粉，素面朝天，形容梅花洁白自然。
glosses.en: qiān huá: face powder. Washing it off means a clean face with no make-up; it shows how pure and natural the white plum flowers look.

glosses.zh: 佳丽：美丽。
glosses.en: jiā lì: beauty.

glosses.zh: 胜赏：尽情欣赏美景。
glosses.en: shèng shǎng: to enjoy a fine sight to the full.

glosses.zh: 孤倚：独自靠着（梅树）。
glosses.en: gū yǐ: to lean alone (against the plum tree).

glosses.zh: 冰盘：洁白如冰的盘子，指宴席上的盘子；一说比喻雪白的梅花。
glosses.en: bīng pán: a plate as white as ice, a dish at the feast. One view says it stands for the snow-white plum flowers themselves.

glosses.zh: 燕喜：宴饮欢乐。
glosses.en: yàn xǐ: to feast and be merry.

glosses.zh: 可惜：这里是可爱的意思。
glosses.en: kě xī: here it means lovely, worth treasuring.

glosses.zh: 香篝：熏香用的竹笼，把衣被盖在上面熏香。这里把雪压梅树比作白被子盖在香笼上。
glosses.en: xiāng gōu: a bamboo cage set over incense, with clothes or quilts laid on top to make them fragrant. Here the snow on the plum tree is like a white quilt over an incense cage.

glosses.zh: 素被：白色的被子，比喻树上的雪。
glosses.en: sù bèi: a white quilt, meaning the snow on the tree.

glosses.zh: 匆匆：急急忙忙，没有多少时间。
glosses.en: cōng cōng: in a hurry, with little time.

glosses.zh: 依依：恋恋不舍的样子。
glosses.en: yī yī: unwilling to part.

glosses.zh: 愁悴：忧愁憔悴。
glosses.en: chóu cuì: sad and worn.

glosses.zh: 吟望：一边吟诗一边观望。
glosses.en: yín wàng: to recite poems while gazing.

glosses.zh: 旋看飞坠：很快就看到花瓣飘落。
glosses.en: xuán kàn fēi zhuì: soon one sees the petals flying down.

glosses.zh: 相将：将要。
glosses.en: xiāng jiāng: about to, soon.

glosses.zh: 脆丸：脆生生的小圆果，指青梅。
glosses.en: cuì wán: crisp little round fruits, that is, green plums.

glosses.zh: 荐酒：用来下酒。
glosses.en: jiàn jiǔ: served with wine.

glosses.zh: 空江烟浪：空阔的江上，烟雾和波浪之间，指词人那时已坐船远去。
glosses.en: kōng jiāng yān làng: on a wide empty river among mist and waves; that is, the poet will have left by boat.

glosses.zh: 潇洒：自然大方、不拘束的样子。
glosses.en: xiāo sǎ: free and graceful.

glosses.zh: 黄昏斜照水：黄昏时梅枝斜斜地映在水里。宋代林逋咏梅有“疏影横斜水清浅”。
glosses.en: huáng hūn xié zhào shuǐ: at dusk the plum branch slants over the water and shows its image there. The Song poet Lin Bu wrote a famous line about sparse plum shadows slanting over clear water.

translation.en: Over the low white wall
the plum blossoms shine bright,
with all their old grace.
Dew is lightly dotted on them,
as if they had washed off their powder,
beautiful beyond words.

translation.zh: 去年我曾独自靠着梅树尽情欣赏，
translation.en: Last year I leaned alone by the tree and enjoyed it to the full,

translation.zh: 还在花前摆宴，一同欢乐。
translation.en: and we feasted happily before the flowers.
Lovelier still
was the tall tree in the snow,

translation.zh: 像香笼上盖着的白被子。
translation.en: like a white quilt laid over an incense cage.
This year I see the flowers in a great hurry.

translation.zh: 相见时花好像也带着怨恨，
translation.en: When we meet, they seem to hold a grudge,

translation.zh: 恋恋不舍，满是忧愁憔悴。
translation.en: clinging, sad and worn.
I recite and gaze for a long time,
and onto the green moss
I soon see petals drifting down.
When the time comes to see

translation.zh: 青梅结果、拿来下酒的时候，
translation.en: green plums served with wine,
I will already be

translation.zh: 空阔江上的烟雾波浪里了。
translation.en: far off among the mist and waves of an empty river.
I can only dream of
that one free and graceful branch

translation.zh: 在黄昏时斜斜地映在水中。
translation.en: slanting over the water at dusk.

background.zh: 这是一首咏梅词，也借梅花写自己的经历。词人去年曾在梅花下欣赏、宴饮，今年再见梅花，却匆匆忙忙，不久就要坐船离开，于是想象日后只能在梦里见到它。一般认为是周邦彦在外地做官、即将离任时写的，具体地点和年份说法不一。
background.en: This is a ci about plum blossoms, and through them the poet writes about his own life. Last year he enjoyed the plum flowers and feasted beneath them. This year he sees them again, but in a hurry, because he must soon leave by boat. So he imagines that later he will see them only in dreams. It is usually thought he wrote it while serving away from the capital, just before leaving his post. The place and year are not agreed.

author_note.zh: 周邦彦（1056—1121），字美成，号清真居士，钱塘（今浙江杭州）人，北宋后期的大词人。他精通音乐，自己创作了不少词调，词的格律非常讲究，被后人看作婉约词的集大成者。他一生在京城和地方之间多次调动，词中常有漂泊和离别的感慨。
author_note.en: Zhou Bangyan (1056–1121), also called Meicheng and Qingzhen, came from Qiantang, today's Hangzhou in Zhejiang. He was a great ci writer of the late Northern Song. He knew music deeply and made many new tunes himself, and his ci follow their rules with great care. Later readers saw him as the master who brought the gentle, graceful style of ci to its peak. He was moved many times between the capital and the provinces, and his ci often carry the feelings of drifting and parting.

appreciation.zh: 这首词有三个时间：现在、过去、将来。开头写眼前：低低的白墙边，梅花耀眼，带着露水，像洗去脂粉的美人。接着回忆去年：独自倚树赏花，花前宴饮，雪中的梅树像盖着白被子的香笼，又美又暖。下阕回到今年：看花太匆忙，花好像也在怨他，依依不舍；他看了很久，花瓣已经飘落到青苔上。最后想到将来：等青梅结果时，自己早已在烟波江上，只能梦见那一枝黄昏里斜映水中的梅花。人和花，一年一年聚散，写尽了漂泊的人对美好事物的留恋。
appreciation.en: This ci moves through three times: now, the past and the future. It opens with the present: by a low white wall, the plum flowers shine, wet with dew, like a beauty who has washed off her powder. Then it remembers last year: leaning alone by the tree, feasting before the flowers, and the snowy tree like a white quilt over an incense cage, lovely and warm. The second stanza returns to this year. He looks in such a hurry that the flowers seem to blame him and cling to him. He gazes for a long time, and the petals are already falling on the moss. At last he looks ahead: when the green plums are ready, he will be far away on a misty river, and can only dream of one branch slanting over the water at dusk. Year after year, the man and the flowers meet and part. It shows how a wanderer holds on to beautiful things.
